title: The same campaign money set against the dates the board actually voted on these vendors’ contracts
question: Measured against recorded votes instead of agenda dates, did these vendors’ staff give to school-board candidates near the votes more often than the campaign calendar alone gives?
finding: No. Against the 48 vendor-vote dates the minutes record, 6 of the 9 vendor-linked contributions fall within 180 days before to 365 days after a vote on that vendor, against 5.9 the campaign calendar gives; 2 within 30 days, against 1.1; 1 of those inside the window went to a sitting member. Against agenda dates (screen vendor-donors-near-board-items) the figures were 6 against 6.0. With 9 contributions the test can show only that nothing stands out.
how: As in vendor-donors-near-board-items, but the board dates are only the vote dates the minutes record for items naming each vendor. The expected count spreads each committee’s own contribution dates over the same windows.
limits: Employer entries are the donors’ own statements and name matches only. Vote dates exist only for the 27 meetings whose minutes are on disk, so a gift near a vote at another meeting is not counted here.
